instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: Moved to Newcastle in February 1998; the same player at both clubs.
Moved to Newcastle in February 1998; the same player at both clubs.
Peak years: a genuinely good all-round left midfielder, outstanding in the air for the position, but never an elite one.
Thirty-four and moved to Bolton; still an ever-present starter and outstanding in the air, but a level below the Newcastle years.
The error-strewn spell that cost him the Liverpool place; a fine shot-stopper with genuinely poor decision-making.
Joined Manchester City in January 2004; the seventeen starts are the half-season, not a drop in ability.
Rated as the 21-year-old Palace midfielder he was, not the England centre-back he became.
Converted to centre-back at Villa and immediately better there than he had been in midfield; England followed.
Captained a League Cup-winning side at 32; reading and organisation still excellent, the pace never having been the point.
Outstanding before a cruciate injury ended his December.
Ankle broken and ligaments damaged in pre-season; returned in January visibly slower. He was not the same footballer again.
Rebuilt as a more static centre-forward: still powerful and a superb finisher, no longer the runner of 1995/96.
Knee trouble and two operations limited him to nineteen starts and five goals. Rated as the player, not the return.
Thirty-three, seven goals in twenty-six starts, and increasingly a static focal point rather than a threat in behind.
Rated as the 18-year-old he was: first-choice wide man in a title side, not the finished player.
At his peak: among the best wide players in Europe in the treble season, even with the appearance total held down by hamstrings.
A converted forward at 18: an outstanding athlete, not yet a good top-flight defender. Rated as he was, not as he became.
Ever-present and an England starter at 21; the point at which he becomes a genuinely good defender.
Twenty-one starts in his last Tottenham season; a knee problem, not a decline.
Four seasons on and at his peak - the best centre-back in the division in the unbeaten season, and in the world conversation.
Sixteen starts: an achilles problem and the Old Trafford walk-off. Still an elite defender, a shade off the previous season.
Arguably the best English goalkeeper in the country in these Leeds seasons, and kept out of the England side rather than out of form.
Twenty-three starts: shared the Champions League season with Paul Robinson rather than lost form.
Thirty-six and the best goalkeeper at Everton by a distance; the two-season gap is a spell out of the side at Leeds, not a decline.
Thirty-nine, moved to Manchester City and retired in January with a shoulder injury. Visibly diminished in his last months.
Cruciate ruptured in September; nine starts. Rated as a good but half-fit player rather than on the peak either side of it.
The reinvention as a deeper, controlling midfielder: the treble season and the Juventus semi-final are the evidence.
Hip surgery in September cost him half the season and a good deal of his mobility; he came back a controlling midfielder rather than a driving one.
Thirty-eight and down to sixteen starts in a West Ham side that went down.
A poor, peripheral first season at United - seven starts and visibly short of confidence.
PFA and FWA Player of the Year at 34: fifteen goals from 23 starts and the link man in a title-winning side. A genuine late peak, not a reputation vote.
Thirty-seven at Portsmouth; the touch and the finishing remain, everything physical has gone.
Split between Newcastle and United by the January transfer; 21 league goals across the two.
Split between Newcastle and United by the January transfer; 21 league goals across the two.
A broken leg and then pneumonia; ten starts, and a player rebuilding rather than performing.
Nineteen goals in 23 starts, the best strike rate of his career, with the link play he had lacked earlier now present.
Fifteen starts as Sheringham and Solskjaer took the shirt; nine goals when he played.
Captain of the title winners; a good, disciplined midfielder rather than a technically special one.
Joined Tottenham in February 1999.
Joined Tottenham in February 1999.
Twenty years old and in and out of the side.
First full season as a starter; quick, powerful and clearly a level up from the fringe player of the year before.
A British record fee for a defender in October 2000; the same player Villa sold, which is the point.
Nine starts at 31; injuries, and Southgate and Riggott ahead of him.
Ever-present at 19 and straight into the Ireland World Cup squad; unusually finished for his age, and he did not improve much on it.
Nineteen and a fringe player.
Straight into the side as an FA Cup-winning starter; the step is a real change in the player, not a re-rating.
Twenty-one and in and out of the side.
Thirty-seven and playing every week for a relegated Wolves side: still the most reliable defender there, but a long way from the United full-back in pace and level.
Three starts - Neil Sullivan took the Tottenham shirt. Rated as the keeper, not on the appearances.
Three seasons on from the last rated one, aged 37 and back from Sporting: still commanding and a fine shot-stopper, but nine points off the peak and no longer near the best in the world.
Wenger's arrival turned a squad player into a first-choice one; the double season is where he becomes genuinely good.
Ten years on from the previous season here: a mature, England-capped midfielder rotating through the unbeaten Arsenal side.
Ruptured a cruciate in April 1997 and managed only 14 starts; rated as the diminished player of that season.
Fully recovered at 34 and Coventry's best player, which earned the Liverpool move.
Thirty-five and the controlling influence on the treble run-in; a fine passer whose game never depended on legs.
The two Inter seasons are absent from the file; he returned to England at essentially the level he left it.
Thirty-five and captain of a relegated Wolves side; the engine that defined him has gone.
First full season as Blackburn’s first-choice left-back; England call-up followed.
The best left-back in the country that season, and a title winner.
Broke an ankle in December; thirteen starts, and he was not the same athlete for over a year.
Six starts through injury.
A clean, positionally sound full-back and Wimbledon's captain; the ceiling is low but the floor is high.
Twenty years old, a double winner and an England starter at Euro 96 within months.
Peak Neville: positionally excellent and an intelligent defender, never an athletic or attacking outlier. Good rather than elite.
A broken foot in the spring; nineteen starts.
Returned to Arsenal from Everton in February 1993.
His peak years: England's man-marker, and the better of the two first-choice Arsenal centre-backs by this point.
Thirty-six and beginning to be rotated; the pace that let him man-mark is going.
Aged 37 and a fringe option by the Invincibles season.
Twenty and already a first-choice wide player, though a raw one.
Settled at West Ham as a direct, two-footed wide player; the level that eventually took him to a World Cup.
Twelve goals at 18 in his first season; already an exceptional finisher, not yet an exceptional footballer.
Twenty-five goals and PFA Young Player; the finishing was already the best in the country.
His peak: 28 league goals at 20, and as pure a finisher as English football produced in the decade. Below Shearer's 91 because the all-round game was narrower.
Cruciate ruptured in February; nineteen starts, and he never regained the movement.
Fifteen starts behind Owen and Heskey, but decisive in the cup treble; the finishing was still the best in the country when he played.
Hip and knee trouble and twelve starts at Manchester City. By 27 the sharpness of movement that made him had gone, and this is where it shows.
Moved to Villa in March 1995; the same player in both halves of the season.
Moved to Villa in March 1995; the same player in both halves of the season.
Thirty-seven, three starts in his final season and a bench option in a double-winning side.
PFA Player of the Year and his peak: 25 goals with the best leap in the division.
Persistent injuries from the Tottenham move onwards; never a first-choice-quality forward again.
Twelve goals from twenty starts in a relegated Leicester side at 36; the leap is still there and almost nothing else is.
Converted from a wide forward into a central one and became a different, better player.
The best season of his career: 18 league goals in a treble side, and among the most complete forwards in Europe that year.
Four starts and out of Ferguson’s plans by Christmas. The fall-off in condition and application was real, not just rotation.
Record fee for a keeper in November 1993; 12 earlier starts for Southampton.
Injured and displaced by John Filan; rated on ability, not on the ten starts.
Joined Blackburn in March 1995 and started the run-in of the title season.
Joined Blackburn in March 1995 and started the run-in of the title season.
Eighteen, three starts; a squad player, and rated as one.
Already the best midfielder at the club at 21, and still nine points short of the 2004/05 anchor (90).
Ever-present in a side that reached a Champions League semi-final; the late-arriving runs and the range of passing are both there, a rung below the 2004/05 anchor.
Fourteen assists and England's first-choice wide player; comfortably his best season.
Six starts. The hernia and hamstring problems that defined the rest of his career start here.
Nineteen and already a regular in a side that finished third; rated as the promising teenager he was, not the 400-game veteran he became.
Eighteen years old and already a 35-start centre-forward; rated as the raw power-and-pace forward he was, not the England career that followed.
A British record fee for a 21-year-old in March; the same player at both clubs.
Fourteen goals in the cup-treble season and an England starter at 22: the best football of his career, and the point where the power and pace were matched by end product.
